purpose: Canonical exam-question archetypes, study cards, and seeded calculation contracts for DSA5101.

archetypes.label: Execute
archetypes.description: Run the algorithm or formula by hand on a small instance.

archetypes.label: Infer
archetypes.description: Infer a guaranteed property, boundary, or failure from the invariant.

archetypes.label: Tune
archetypes.description: Predict how a parameter changes error, precision, recall, or runtime.

archetypes.label: Choose
archetypes.description: Choose a method and justify it from scale, representation, and objective.

cards.title: Scale: passes, memory, and approximation
cards.objective: Compare algorithms using passes, working memory, and the error contract.

cards.title: Assessment format and weights
cards.objective: Identify the official assessment weights and separate course evidence from study priority.

cards.title: Support, confidence, and lift denominators
cards.objective: Keep basket support, conditional confidence, and baseline lift separate.

cards.title: Apriori: subset, superset, and downward closure
cards.objective: Use an infrequent itemset to prune every superset, never a subset.

cards.title: Apriori: generate $C_k$ and prune to $L_k$
cards.objective: Join only compatible frequent $(k-1)$-itemsets, then remove candidates with an infrequent subset.

cards.title: PCY: bucket counts across two passes
cards.objective: Separate frequent items from frequent hash buckets before counting candidate pairs.

cards.title: Shingles as sets and Jaccard similarity
cards.objective: Deduplicate shingles within each document before computing set Jaccard.

cards.title: Characteristic matrix to MinHash signature
cards.objective: Evaluate the minimum permuted row for each hash function and column.

cards.title: MinHash collision versus Jaccard
cards.objective: Use one-row collision probability $s$ and do not confuse it with a whole signature or LSH candidate event.

cards.title: LSH: row, band, and whole-signature probabilities
cards.objective: Compute $s^r$ for one band and $1-(1-s^r)^b$ for at least one matching band.

cards.title: LSH tuning: bands, rows, precision, and recall
cards.objective: Recognize that more bands make the OR candidate event easier and usually raise recall while admitting more false positives.

cards.title: LSH candidate verification
cards.objective: Treat a band collision as a candidate signal and verify exact Jaccard before claiming similarity.

cards.title: Hierarchical clustering: single, complete, and average linkage
cards.objective: Recompute the distance between clusters using the stated linkage, not a remembered default.

cards.title: K-means assignment and centroid update
cards.objective: Alternate nearest-centroid assignment with the mean update while tracking the squared-error objective.

cards.title: BFR and CURE summaries
cards.objective: Classify discard, compression, retained, and representative-point states by what information they preserve.

cards.title: Clustering evaluation and purity limits
cards.objective: Interpret purity with cluster count and distinguish external-label scores from intrinsic utility.

cards.title: User-based recommendation: center ratings before cosine
cards.objective: Subtract each user mean on the shared items before comparing rating direction.

cards.title: Neighbour overlap and weighted prediction
cards.objective: Use only shared rated items and keep the similarity weighting denominator explicit.

cards.title: Latent-factor prediction
cards.objective: Distinguish a dot-product prediction from a neighbourhood estimate.

cards.title: PageRank transition orientation and power iteration
cards.objective: Fix row- versus column-stochastic convention before multiplying the rank vector.

cards.title: PageRank teleportation and dangling nodes
cards.objective: Redistribute teleport or leaked mass using the convention stated in the problem.

cards.title: DGIM: recent-window query and oldest bucket
cards.objective: Use the oldest partially covered bucket for the boundary estimate and expose its error bound.

cards.title: Flajolet–Martin versus AMS moments
cards.objective: Match distinct-count sketches to $F_0$ and frequency-moment sketches to $F_k$.

cards.title: BALANCE: budget trace and tie-breaking
cards.objective: Track remaining budgets and state the tie rule before claiming a BALANCE outcome or guarantee.

cards.title: Dimensionality reduction: SVD and rank
cards.objective: Use singular values to reason about latent directions, retained energy, and low-rank error.

cards.title: CUR versus SVD representations
cards.objective: Choose between dense latent factors and actual sampled rows or columns using the stated objective.

cards.title: Communities: conductance and PPR sweep
cards.objective: Normalize a cut, order PPR scores by degree, and distinguish a local community from a global optimum.

cards.title: PageRank, TrustRank, and spam mass
cards.objective: Separate ordinary link importance from trusted teleportation and spam-mass comparisons.

cards.title: Decision trees: entropy and information gain
cards.objective: Evaluate candidate thresholds with parent entropy minus size-weighted child entropy.

cards.title: Submodularity: diminishing returns and greedy coverage
cards.objective: Test diminishing returns and select the next set by marginal coverage, not raw size.

cards.title: Bandits: empirical means, exploration, and regret
cards.objective: Update arm statistics, compute exploration probabilities, and separate reward from regret.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose a scalable design for data that does not fit in main memory.
templates.assumptions: The input is large enough that I/O passes and bounded working memory matter.
templates.coreInvariant: A memory claim is incomplete without the number of passes and the error contract.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compare passes, peak memory, shuffle, and approximation before comparing constant factors.
failureModes: Treating equal asymptotic time as equal external-memory cost.
Reporting memory savings without stating approximation.
templates.examMove: Name the dominant resource first, then justify the method by its state and pass count.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute the fraction of baskets containing an itemset.
templates.assumptions: Support is normalized by the total number of baskets.
templates.coreInvariant: The numerator counts qualifying baskets and the denominator counts all baskets.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\operatorname{supp}(I)=\frac{\#\{B:I\subseteq B\}}{\#\{B\}}$$
failureModes: Using the number of baskets containing a premise as the support denominator.
Confusing support with confidence.
templates.examMove: Write the two counts before reducing the fraction.

templates.problemDefinition: Interpret the conditional probability represented by a rule $A\to B$.
templates.assumptions: The rule is evaluated among baskets that contain $A$.
templates.coreInvariant: Confidence conditions on the antecedent.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\operatorname{conf}(A\to B)=\frac{\operatorname{supp}(A\cup B)}{\operatorname{supp}(A)}$$
failureModes: Dividing by the total basket count.
Treating high confidence as proof of causality.
templates.examMove: Underline the condition in the English sentence and use it as the denominator.

templates.problemDefinition: Infer which candidates can be discarded from an infrequent itemset.
templates.assumptions: Support is measured over sets of items and adding items cannot create new containing baskets.
templates.coreInvariant: $I\subseteq J$ implies $\operatorname{supp}(I)\geq\operatorname{supp}(J)$.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: If $I$ is infrequent, prune every superset $J\supseteq I$; do not prune subsets.
failureModes: Reversing subset and superset.
Using downward closure to make a claim about confidence or independence.
templates.examMove: Draw the containment arrow and move from the infrequent set upward.

templates.problemDefinition: Construct $C_k$ from $L_{k-1}$ and prune candidates with an infrequent $(k-1)$-subset.
templates.assumptions: Itemsets are sorted and the previous level $L_{k-1}$ is complete.
templates.coreInvariant: Every $(k-1)$-subset of a frequent $k$-itemset must itself be frequent.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Join compatible members of $L_{k-1}$, then retain only candidates whose every $(k-1)$-subset is in $L_{k-1}$.
failureModes: Keeping a join whose subset was already pruned.
Generating candidates from arbitrary baskets instead of $L_{k-1}$.
templates.examMove: List the join, enumerate all immediate subsets, and cross-check membership in $L_{k-1}$.

templates.problemDefinition: Trace PCY's first-pass counts and second-pass candidate filter.
templates.assumptions: The bucket bit-vector records whether a pair-count bucket reaches support threshold.
templates.coreInvariant: A pair is a second-pass candidate only if both items are frequent and its bucket is frequent.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Pass 1 counts singleton items and hashed pair buckets; pass 2 counts pairs satisfying both filters.
failureModes: Treating a frequent bucket as proof that every pair in it is frequent.
Forgetting that hash collisions create false candidates, not false negatives for a truly counted pair.
templates.examMove: Apply the item test and bucket test separately for every pair.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute similarity of two documents represented by shingle sets.
templates.assumptions: Repeated occurrences of the same shingle collapse to one set member.
templates.coreInvariant: Jaccard is intersection divided by union over unique shingles.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$J(A,B)=\frac{|A\cap B|}{|A\cup B|}$$
failureModes: Counting repeated shingles as separate multiset entries.
Using the sum of set sizes as the union when the intersection is nonempty.
templates.examMove: Deduplicate first, then compute intersection and union.

templates.problemDefinition: Evaluate a MinHash signature from a characteristic matrix and row permutations.
templates.assumptions: The minimum permuted row containing a 1 is taken independently for each hash function and column.
templates.coreInvariant: The probability that one MinHash row agrees equals the Jaccard similarity.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: For each column and permutation, scan the permutation until the first row containing a 1.
failureModes: Taking the minimum row index in the original order for every hash.
Comparing raw characteristic columns instead of signatures.
templates.examMove: Write the permutation order down the side and stop at the first 1 in each column.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute a collision probability at one MinHash row.
templates.assumptions: The hash permutation is uniform and the two sets have Jaccard similarity $s$.
templates.coreInvariant: One-row MinHash collision probability is $s$, not $s^r$ or $1-(1-s^r)^b$.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$P(\text{one row agrees})=s$$
failureModes: Calling $s$ the probability of a whole LSH candidate.
Multiplying by the number of rows without checking which event is asked.
templates.examMove: Name the event before choosing the formula: row, band, or any band.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute the probability that two signatures become an LSH candidate.
templates.assumptions: Rows within a band and bands are treated as independent for the classroom model.
templates.coreInvariant: A band matches only when all $r$ rows match; the candidate event is an OR across $b$ bands.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$P(\text{candidate})=1-(1-s^r)^b$$
failureModes: Using $s^r$ for the entire LSH candidate event.
Adding band probabilities directly and exceeding 1.
Confusing a row collision with a band collision.
templates.examMove: Build the AND inside one band first, then the OR across bands.

templates.problemDefinition: Predict how changing the number of bands affects candidate generation.
templates.assumptions: The signature length and row count per band are otherwise held fixed or the comparison states the new $r$ explicitly.
templates.coreInvariant: Increasing $b$ makes the OR event easier when $r$ is held fixed.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$1-(1-s^r)^b$$ increases with $b$ for $0<s<1$ and fixed $r$.
failureModes: Claiming more bands automatically raises precision.
Changing $b$ while silently changing the total signature length.
templates.examMove: Check whether the question holds $r$ or total rows fixed, then reason about the OR threshold.

templates.problemDefinition: Translate an LSH collision event into Boolean structure.
templates.assumptions: A row match is the atomic event.
templates.coreInvariant: Rows within a band are ANDed; bands are ORed; exact verification is a later stage.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: AND within band, OR across bands, then exact candidate verification.
failureModes: Applying OR within a band.
Treating candidate generation as exact classification.
templates.examMove: Write AND–OR–AND beside the question before selecting a probability or claim.

templates.problemDefinition: Decide what an LSH collision justifies before an exact similarity or equality check.
templates.assumptions: LSH is used as a candidate-generation filter and may produce false positives.
templates.coreInvariant: A candidate signal is weaker than an exact duplicate or similarity guarantee.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Generate candidates with LSH, then verify exact Jaccard or exact set equality when the application requires it.
failureModes: Treating one band collision as proof of duplicate documents.
Replacing the exact verifier with a band key.
templates.examMove: Separate candidate generation from the application-level acceptance rule.

templates.problemDefinition: Recompute a cluster-to-point distance after a merge.
templates.assumptions: The question names single, complete, or average linkage and supplies the relevant pairwise distances.
templates.coreInvariant: The linkage definition, not the dendrogram shape, determines the new distance.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Single uses a minimum, complete a maximum, and average the mean over cross-cluster pairs.
failureModes: Using the nearest pair for every linkage.
Treating a merge height as a centroid distance.
templates.examMove: Write the named reducer before reading the numbers.

templates.problemDefinition: Recompute one K-means centroid from its assigned points.
templates.assumptions: The assignment step is already fixed and the Euclidean mean is the representative.
templates.coreInvariant: The centroid minimizes the sum of squared distances for the fixed assignment.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$z=\frac{1}{|C|}\sum_{x\in C}x$$
failureModes: Using a median for ordinary K-means.
Updating the centroid before fixing the assignment set.
templates.examMove: List assigned points, sum coordinates, and divide by the cluster count.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose a scalable cluster summary when one centroid would hide shape or outliers.
templates.assumptions: The data arrives in chunks and memory cannot retain every point.
templates.coreInvariant: BFR stores sufficient statistics for confident clusters; CURE keeps dispersed representatives shrunk toward the mean.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Choose DS, CS, RS, or representative points from certainty, shape, and outlier evidence.
failureModes: Calling every unassigned point a discard-set member.
Assuming one centroid preserves a non-spherical cluster.
templates.examMove: Classify the point or summary by confidence and shape before naming the data structure.

templates.problemDefinition: Compare users by rating pattern rather than absolute rating level.
templates.assumptions: Only co-rated items are used and each user is centered by their mean over those items.
templates.coreInvariant: Cosine is applied to centered vectors, not raw ratings, for this user-based method.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\cos(u,v)=\frac{(r_u-\bar r_u)\cdot(r_v-\bar r_v)}{\|r_u-\bar r_u\|\,\|r_v-\bar r_v\|}$$
failureModes: Skipping centering.
Including non-overlapping items in the dot product.
templates.examMove: Write both means and centered vectors before taking the cosine.

templates.problemDefinition: Predict a target rating from mean-centered neighbour deviations.
templates.assumptions: Only neighbours who rated the target item contribute and the denominator is the sum of the contributing similarities.
templates.coreInvariant: The prediction starts at the target user's mean and adds a normalized similarity-weighted deviation.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\hat r_{ui}=\bar r_u+\frac{\sum_{v\in N(u)}s_{uv}(r_{vi}-\bar r_v)}{\sum_{v\in N(u)}s_{uv}}$$
failureModes: Using raw ratings instead of deviations from each neighbour mean.
Omitting the similarity normalization denominator.
templates.examMove: Center each neighbour, accumulate weighted deviations, then divide before adding the target baseline.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose between neighbourhood and latent-factor predictions.
templates.assumptions: The prompt distinguishes learned user/item vectors from local rating overlap.
templates.coreInvariant: A latent-factor prediction is a dot product of learned vectors, not a weighted neighbour average.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\hat r_{ui}=q_u\cdot p_i$$
failureModes: Using a neighbourhood denominator for a latent dot product.
Calling a dot product a similarity without identifying the learned factors.
templates.examMove: Identify whether the inputs are neighbours and ratings or learned vectors.

templates.problemDefinition: Apply one PageRank transition update using the stated matrix convention.
templates.assumptions: The transition matrix is explicitly declared row- or column-stochastic and dangling nodes are handled separately.
templates.coreInvariant: The multiplication orientation must preserve probability mass under the declared stochastic convention.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: For a column-stochastic matrix, $$r^{(t+1)}=Mr^{(t)}$$; for a row-stochastic matrix, use the matching row-vector convention.
failureModes: Transposing the matrix silently.
Assuming row-stochastic because rows are easier to read.
templates.examMove: Label the vector orientation and check the matrix sums before multiplying.

templates.problemDefinition: Update PageRank when teleportation or leaked mass is present.
templates.assumptions: The teleport set, damping convention, and dangling-node rule are stated in the prompt.
templates.coreInvariant: Every iteration must account for link-following mass plus all injected or leaked probability.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$r=\beta Mr+(1-\beta)v$$
failureModes: Adding uniform teleport mass when teleport is topic-specific.
Dropping rank from a dangling node.
templates.examMove: Write the bias vector $v$ before applying the damping factor.

templates.problemDefinition: Estimate the number of recent 1s in a DGIM window.
templates.assumptions: At most two buckets of each size are stored and the query boundary cuts the oldest bucket.
templates.coreInvariant: All fully covered buckets are counted exactly; the oldest partial bucket exposes the approximation interval.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Include one-half of the oldest boundary bucket in the classroom estimate; the additive uncertainty is bounded by that bucket size.
failureModes: Treating the oldest bucket as fully inside the query.
Choosing the newest bucket as the uncertain one.
templates.examMove: Order buckets by timestamp, mark the query boundary, and only then sum sizes.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose the sketch whose target matches a streaming query.
templates.assumptions: The query asks either for distinct values or a frequency moment.
templates.coreInvariant: Flajolet–Martin targets a distinct count $F_0$; AMS targets a frequency moment such as $F_2=\sum_i f_i^2$.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Match the estimator to the target statistic before discussing memory or error.
failureModes: Calling $F_0$ the total number of stream elements.
Calling $F_2$ the number of distinct elements.
templates.examMove: Write the target symbol and its definition before selecting a sketch.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute a second frequency moment from a small frequency table.
templates.assumptions: The frequencies $f_i$ are exact for the worked instance.
templates.coreInvariant: The zeroth moment counts distinct values, while $F_2$ squares each frequency.
failureModes: Returning the total number of observations.
Returning the number of distinct keys.
templates.examMove: Write one squared term per key before summing.

templates.problemDefinition: Trace BALANCE's remaining budgets and allocation on a query sequence.
templates.assumptions: Only eligible advertisers bid and the rule chooses the eligible advertiser with larger remaining budget.
templates.coreInvariant: After assignment, exactly the chosen advertiser's remaining budget decreases by one.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$B_t(a)=B_{t-1}(a)-1$$ for the advertiser selected at time $t$.
failureModes: Choosing the largest original budget instead of the current budget.
Forgetting that eligibility changes the comparison set.
templates.examMove: Write the full state before each query and update one coordinate only.

templates.problemDefinition: Decide whether a BALANCE outcome is determined when remaining budgets tie.
templates.assumptions: The tie-breaking policy must be explicit before comparing online and offline allocations.
templates.coreInvariant: A guarantee quantifies over every allowed tie resolution; one favourable trace is only a possible outcome.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: State the tie rule, simulate each relevant branch, then compare against the offline optimum.
failureModes: Ignoring ties.
Claiming a guarantee from one tie resolution.
templates.examMove: Circle every tie and branch before writing a guarantee claim.

templates.problemDefinition: Run a parameterized PCY first-pass bucket filter and second-pass candidate check.
templates.assumptions: The pair hash, support threshold, singleton counts, and bucket counts are supplied.
templates.coreInvariant: A candidate pair needs two frequent items and a frequent hash bucket; the exact second pass still decides frequency.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Count singletons and buckets, set the bitmap, then retain pairs satisfying the item-and-bucket conjunction.
failureModes: Treating a frequent bucket as proof of a frequent pair.
Skipping the singleton test.
templates.examMove: Mark the singleton predicate and bucket predicate in separate columns before intersecting them.

templates.problemDefinition: Run a parameterized MinHash signature calculation on a small characteristic matrix.
templates.assumptions: Rows are labeled from one and the stated permutation lists row labels in scan order.
templates.coreInvariant: Each signature entry is the first permuted row containing a one in that column.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Scan each permutation independently for each column and record the first matching row label.
failureModes: Scanning the original row order instead of the permutation.
Confusing a row label with a permutation position.
templates.examMove: Write the permutation sequence explicitly, then cross out rows after the first one.

templates.problemDefinition: Select bands and rows that satisfy high-similarity recall and low-similarity false-positive constraints.
templates.assumptions: The total signature length is fixed and the independent banding model applies.
templates.coreInvariant: For each candidate $(b,r)$, evaluate $1-(1-s^r)^b$ at both similarity targets.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Enumerate factor pairs of $m=br$, test the high and low similarity inequalities, and reject pairs that violate either bound.
failureModes: Optimizing only the high-similarity probability.
Changing $b$ without preserving $br$.
templates.examMove: Build a divisor table; do not guess from the S-curve alone.

templates.problemDefinition: Select a K-means stopping and initialization outcome from the parameterized Lloyd iterations.
templates.assumptions: Euclidean distance is used, ties go to the lower-index centroid, and an empty cluster keeps its previous centroid.
templates.coreInvariant: Each assignment/update round does not increase the squared-error objective for fixed conventions, but initialization can change the local result.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Enumerate the assignment/update rounds for the stated initialization, then stop when assignments no longer change.
failureModes: Updating with the old assignment after reassignment.
Treating convergence as a global optimum or ignoring initialization.
templates.examMove: Keep a round table with assignments, centroids, and the stop condition; compare another initialization when the question asks about tuning.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute one rating from learned user and item latent vectors.
templates.assumptions: The factors are already learned and the stated model has no extra bias term.
templates.coreInvariant: The prediction is the dot product of the matching user and item vectors.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\hat r_{ui}=q_u\cdot p_i=\sum_k q_{uk}p_{ik}$$
failureModes: Using a neighbourhood similarity denominator.
Pairing a user vector with the wrong item vector.
templates.examMove: Align coordinates by factor index, multiply pairwise, and sum once.

templates.problemDefinition: Apply a column-stochastic PageRank operator twice and read one resulting coordinate.
templates.assumptions: The matrix is column-stochastic, no teleportation is used, and the rank vector is a column vector.
templates.coreInvariant: Each iteration conserves total probability under the declared orientation.
failureModes: Applying the matrix only once when the question asks for two iterations.
Transposing a column-stochastic matrix without changing the vector convention.
templates.examMove: Compute and label $r^{(1)}$ before using it to compute $r^{(2)}$.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute the one-register Flajolet–Martin distinct-count estimate from a maximum zero-prefix.
templates.assumptions: The classroom one-register estimate uses $2^R$ and ignores averaging or bias correction.
templates.coreInvariant: The longest trailing-zero run is evidence about the number of distinct hashed values, not stream length.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\widehat F_0=2^R$$
failureModes: Calling $2^R$ an exact distinct count.
Using $R$ instead of $2^R$.
templates.examMove: Name the target $F_0$, then exponentiate the observed run length.

templates.problemDefinition: Evaluate one AMS second-moment variable from a sampled suffix count.
templates.assumptions: The stream length $n$, sampled value count $X$, and classroom estimator are supplied.
templates.coreInvariant: The estimator is unbiased in expectation even though one sample is noisy.
failureModes: Using $nX$ as the estimator.
Confusing an AMS sample with the exact $F_2$.
templates.examMove: Compute the odd factor $2X-1$ first, then multiply by $n$.

templates.problemDefinition: Recover a singular value from an eigenvalue of $A^TA$.
templates.assumptions: The supplied eigenvalue is non-negative and corresponds to the requested singular direction.
templates.coreInvariant: The singular value is the non-negative square root of the matching eigenvalue.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$A^TA v_i=\lambda_i v_i,\qquad \sigma_i=\sqrt{\lambda_i}$$
failureModes: Using $\lambda_i$ as the singular value.
Taking a negative square root.
templates.examMove: Label whether the number belongs to $\Sigma^2$ or $\Sigma$ before taking the root.

templates.problemDefinition: Select a retained rank and compute the squared Frobenius error from the discarded singular directions.
templates.assumptions: Singular values are ordered and the best rank-$k$ approximation is used.
templates.coreInvariant: Increasing retained rank removes tail energy from the low-rank reconstruction error.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\lVert A-A_k\rVert_F^2=\sum_{i>k}\sigma_i^2$$
failureModes: Summing retained rather than discarded energy.
Taking a square root when the question asks for squared error or ignoring the rank trade-off.
templates.examMove: Draw a line after $\sigma_k$, square only the tail, and compare candidate ranks when tuning.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose a dimensionality-reduction representation from sparsity and interpretability requirements.
templates.assumptions: The task permits approximation and explicitly values either latent directions or actual data rows and columns.
templates.coreInvariant: SVD uses latent factors; CUR uses sampled columns and rows from the original matrix.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compare $A\approx U\Sigma V^T$ with $A\approx CUR$ using error, sparsity, and interpretability.
failureModes: Calling $C$ and $R$ learned latent vectors.
Assuming CUR is the exact best rank-$k$ approximation.
templates.examMove: Underline whether the output must remain interpretable as original rows or columns.

templates.problemDefinition: Score a candidate community using its cut and the volumes of both sides.
templates.assumptions: The graph is undirected for the conductance calculation and volumes are supplied.
templates.coreInvariant: Conductance normalizes the cut by the smaller side volume.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\phi(S)= rac{\operatorname{cut}(S, ar S)}{\min(\operatorname{vol}(S),\operatorname{vol}( ar S))}$$
failureModes: Using cut size alone.
Dividing by the larger volume by habit.
templates.examMove: Compute both volumes, choose the smaller denominator, then divide.

templates.problemDefinition: Order vertices for a personalized-PageRank sweep before comparing prefix conductance.
templates.assumptions: The sweep score is $p(v)/d(v)$ and ties use the stated vertex order.
templates.coreInvariant: The sweep ordering is by normalized PPR score, not raw PPR alone.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compute $p(v)/d(v)$, sort descending, and evaluate conductance of prefix sets.
failureModes: Sorting by raw PPR when degrees differ.
Choosing the largest prefix without evaluating conductance.
templates.examMove: Write one normalized score column before sorting vertices.

templates.problemDefinition: Interpret what Louvain convergence does and does not guarantee.
templates.assumptions: The algorithm accepts only local modularity-improving moves under its current ordering.
templates.coreInvariant: Accepted local moves improve the current modularity, but the final partition need not be globally optimal.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Repeat local moves and aggregation until no accepted move improves the objective.
failureModes: Equating convergence with global optimality.
Ignoring dependence on initialization or node order.
templates.examMove: Separate monotonic local improvement from a global optimality claim.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose whether ordinary PageRank or TrustRank is the appropriate comparison for suspected web spam.
templates.assumptions: A trusted seed set is available and the question asks about trust propagation rather than popularity alone.
templates.coreInvariant: TrustRank changes the teleport preference to trusted seeds; it is not just a second name for PageRank.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compare standard teleportation with a trusted teleport vector, then inspect relative spam mass.
failureModes: Using indegree as a trust score.
Treating a trusted seed set as a universal popularity prior.
templates.examMove: Identify the teleport vector before interpreting the ranking.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute the class entropy at a decision-tree node.
templates.assumptions: The node counts are non-negative and the logarithm is base two.
templates.coreInvariant: Entropy measures class uncertainty before a split.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$H(Y)=-\sum_c p_c\log_2p_c$$
failureModes: Using raw counts as probabilities.
Forgetting the negative sign or the base-two convention.
templates.examMove: Convert counts to proportions first, then sum one term per class.

templates.problemDefinition: Compare a candidate threshold using parent entropy minus weighted child entropy.
templates.assumptions: The split partitions every example into exactly one child and uses the same impurity measure on all nodes.
templates.coreInvariant: Information gain is the uncertainty removed by the split, weighted by child sizes.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$IG=H(Y)- rac{N_L}{N}H(Y_L)- rac{N_R}{N}H(Y_R)$$
failureModes: Forgetting child-size weights.
Choosing the split with the largest raw child count instead of gain.
templates.examMove: Compute parent, left, and right entropy separately before subtracting.

templates.problemDefinition: Test a set function for diminishing returns using two nested sets.
templates.assumptions: The candidate element is outside the larger set and the function is evaluated on finite sets.
templates.coreInvariant: For $A\subseteq B$, the marginal gain of adding $x$ to $A$ is at least the marginal gain of adding $x$ to $B$.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$f(A\cup\{x\})-f(A)\geq f(B\cup\{x\})-f(B)$$
failureModes: Reversing the inequality.
Checking only monotonicity instead of diminishing returns.
templates.examMove: Write both marginal gains explicitly; do not compare total values only.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose the next set in a maximum-coverage greedy run from current marginal gains.
templates.assumptions: The objective is monotone coverage and the budget is a fixed number of set selections.
templates.coreInvariant: Greedy chooses the largest uncovered marginal gain at every step, not the largest raw set.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$S^*=\arg\max_S|S\setminus Covered|$$
failureModes: Choosing the largest raw set after overlap appears.
Recomputing gain against the empty covered set every round.
templates.examMove: Cross out already covered elements before comparing candidate gains.

templates.problemDefinition: Update an arm's empirical mean from its observed reward history.
templates.assumptions: Only rewards from the named arm count and each observation has equal weight.
templates.coreInvariant: The empirical mean uses the arm's own observed rewards divided by its pull count.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$\widehat\mu_i= rac{1}{N_i}\sum_{t:a_t=i}r_t$$
failureModes: Averaging rewards from other arms.
Dividing by the total number of rounds instead of arm pulls.
templates.examMove: Filter the history by arm before summing or dividing.

templates.problemDefinition: Compute the next-round probability of selecting the empirically best arm under epsilon-greedy.
templates.assumptions: Exploration is uniform over $K$ arms and exploitation selects one unique best arm.
templates.coreInvariant: The best arm receives exploitation probability plus its share of exploration probability.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$P(\text{best})=1-\epsilon+\frac{\epsilon}{K}$$
failureModes: Giving the best arm probability $1-\epsilon$ only.
Dividing exploration by the number of non-best arms.
templates.examMove: Write exploitation and exploration as two separate terms before adding them.

templates.problemDefinition: Evaluate an upper-confidence-bound score that balances empirical reward and uncertainty.
templates.assumptions: The prompt fixes the exploration constant and uses natural logarithms.
templates.coreInvariant: The uncertainty bonus decreases as an arm is sampled more often and increases with the time horizon.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: $$UCB_i(t)=\widehat\mu_i+c\sqrt{ rac{\ln t}{N_i}}$$
failureModes: Dropping the exploration bonus.
Using total pulls in place of the arm-specific $N_i$.
templates.examMove: Calculate the bonus separately, then add it to the empirical mean.

templates.problemDefinition: Interpret a lower trusted score for a suspected spam region after changing the teleport set.
templates.assumptions: The trusted teleport set is chosen outside the suspected spam region and the graph operator is otherwise unchanged.
templates.coreInvariant: TrustRank reduces the influence of untrusted regions by changing where teleport mass enters.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compare standard and trusted rank mass on the spam set under the same link-following convention.
failureModes: Calling lower TrustRank evidence that the pages have no incoming links.
Changing both the graph and teleport vector in the comparison.
templates.examMove: Hold the transition graph fixed and attribute the change to the teleport preference.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose a decision-tree split and stopping policy from impurity reduction and generalization risk.
templates.assumptions: The candidate split is evaluated on training data, and validation evidence is available for model selection.
templates.coreInvariant: Information gain measures training impurity reduction; it does not by itself guarantee lower validation error.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compare candidate splits with weighted child entropy, then use validation or regularization to control depth.
failureModes: Selecting the deepest tree solely by training gain.
Using unweighted child entropy for information gain.
templates.examMove: Separate the split score from the stopping or pruning decision.

templates.problemDefinition: Choose an exploration policy when empirical means are uncertain and future reward matters.
templates.assumptions: Arms have different unknown reward distributions and the learner observes reward only for the selected arm.
templates.coreInvariant: Exploration reduces uncertainty while exploitation uses current estimates; a policy must trade both over time.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Compare epsilon-greedy, UCB, or related policies through their exploration term and regret behavior.
failureModes: Always selecting the current empirical winner.
Exploring uniformly without accounting for uncertainty or pull count.
templates.examMove: Identify whether the policy explicitly prices uncertainty before claiming low regret.

templates.problemDefinition: Identify the official assessment format and weighting from the course information sheet.
templates.assumptions: The question asks about documented course information, not an unverified final-exam prediction.
templates.coreInvariant: Assessment facts and study priorities must remain separate claims.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Read the source-backed assessment table, compare weights, and report unknown scope as unknown.
failureModes: Treating an A+ study priority as an official exam guarantee.
Comparing a pending date or scope as if it were confirmed.
templates.examMove: Name the source and fact type before ranking assessment components.

templates.problemDefinition: Interpret an external clustering score together with its cluster-count and task context.
templates.assumptions: Purity is computed from supplied labels and may be inflated by singleton clusters.
templates.coreInvariant: A high purity score alone does not establish intrinsic geometry or downstream usefulness.
templates.formulaAlgorithm: Report purity with the number of clusters and add an intrinsic or task-specific metric before making a stronger claim.
failureModes: Equating purity one with a useful clustering.
Ignoring the cluster count and external-label dependence.
templates.examMove: Check what labels and cluster count produced the score before interpreting it.
